title: Prime-factor advice in power-residue quotients
exact_target: For a given prime $p$, how much auxiliary data suffices to reduce the solution of higher-degree equations modulo $p$ to an efficient computation, in analogy with a single quadratic nonresidue for quadratic equations? Does a deterministic subexponential-time algorithm find a quadratic nonresidue modulo $p$ without an unproved hypothesis?
